answer.headline: Large hubs show no established link between top-carrier seat share and departure delay, and high-delay hubs are not concentration anomalies
answer.body:
Across FAA large hubs, largest operating-carrier seat share and departure delay rate were compared airport by airport for {F99.period}. The calculated Pearson correlation is {F61}. The calculated Spearman rank correlation is {F62}. The bootstrap interval for the Spearman correlation runs from {F63} to {F64} and uses {F65}. That interval includes negative and positive values, so the sign of the rank association is not established. These figures are calculated associations across airports. They are not a forecast, and they do not show that carrier concentration causes delay.

High-delay hubs are the large hubs whose departure delay rate sits above {F99} ({F99.label}). Those delay rates are FLL {F42}, DFW {F39}, BNA {F33}, BWI {F35}, DCA {F37}, ORD {F53}, MCO {F50}, and LAS {F47}. Top-carrier seat shares in that set are FLL {F143}, DFW {F142}, BNA {F139}, BWI {F140}, DCA {F141}, ORD {F146}, MCO {F145}, and LAS {F144}. The median top-carrier seat share in the high-delay set is {F165}, the median across all large hubs is {F200}, and the high-delay median minus the all-large-hub median is {F203}.

Descriptive robust z-scores of seat share inside the high-delay set are FLL {F151}, DFW {F150}, BNA {F147}, BWI {F148}, DCA {F149}, ORD {F154}, MCO {F153}, and LAS {F152}. A cross-section anomaly screen at the catalog default robust-z threshold flagged no airport for top-carrier seat share inside that set. The same default screen flagged no large hub for departure delay rate and no large hub for top-carrier seat share. The z-scores above were recorded by retaining every hub in the set. They are calculated scores. The operator caveat that calls each an outlier relative to the set is not an anomaly flag. High delay in this answer is the upper-quartile cut, not a set of delay outliers.

claims.text: For {F99.period}, the calculated Pearson correlation of top-carrier seat share and departure delay rate across large hubs is {F61}, the calculated Spearman rank correlation is {F62}, and the Spearman bootstrap interval runs from {F63} to {F64}, using {F65}.

The Spearman interval includes negative and positive values, so the sign of the rank association is not established. The result is a calculated cross-airport association and does not show that carrier concentration causes delay.
Large hubs above {F99} ({F99.label}) are FLL {F42}, DFW {F39}, BNA {F33}, BWI {F35}, DCA {F37}, ORD {F53}, MCO {F50}, and LAS {F47}.

Top-carrier seat shares in that high-delay set are FLL {F143}, DFW {F142}, BNA {F139}, BWI {F140}, DCA {F141}, ORD {F146}, MCO {F145}, and LAS {F144}. The high-delay median is {F165}, the all-large-hub median is {F200}, and the calculated gap is {F203}.
Descriptive robust z-scores of top-carrier seat share inside the high-delay set are FLL {F151}, DFW {F150}, BNA {F147}, BWI {F148}, DCA {F149}, ORD {F154}, MCO {F153}, and LAS {F152}.

The catalog default robust-z screen flagged no airport for top-carrier seat share inside the high-delay set, and it flagged no large hub for departure delay rate or for top-carrier seat share. The z-scores are descriptive scores from a screen that retains every hub in the set, not anomaly flags. High delay here is the upper-quartile cut rather than a delay-outlier set.
Carrier concentration could still relate to delay through gates, schedules, or local operations, but this cross-section does not identify a cause.

assumptions: Large hubs means the FAA large-hub class in the catalog group filter. The phrase large hubs did not resolve as a place name.
High-delay means a large hub whose departure delay rate is above {F99.label} during {F99.period}.
Seat share and delay rate use that same window, the months covered by both T-100 seats and on-time departures.
Descriptive robust z-scores retain every airport in the high-delay set. The anomaly test itself uses the catalog default threshold.
limitations: Departure delay rate covers domestic flights of reporting carriers only. Top-carrier seat share uses T-100 departing passenger and combi segments, including international flying, so the series do not describe the same traffic.
The correlation does not control for airport size, region, season, or weather. It is not a forecast.
No large hub met the default robust-z rule on delay rate, so high delay cannot be defined as a statistical delay outlier. The upper-quartile cut is an assumption.
The concentration test inside the high-delay set compares each hub with the other hubs in that set. A separate default screen of top-carrier seat share on all large hubs also returned no flags.
The default screen emits a finding only for a flagged airport, so an empty screen is the operator result rather than a stored count of anomalies.
On-time coverage runs through August 2026, while T-100 seats in this extract end in July 2026. The shared window stops where both series exist.
Unmet demand, terminal capacity, fares, and profitability are not measured. This is not an investment screen and not a valuation.
